description: CPU and wall time of exporting video R at each optimization step. Two measurement windows: the first two steps were measured on a 15 s segment, the last three on the whole video. Do not divide numbers across windows.
video_R: R: 75 s production video, presenter footage plus motion graphics, rendered at 1080x1920 and 1920x1080. Presenter footage is 1920x1080 H.264 at 25 fps.
metric: CPU = user+sys of the systemd scope cgroup (includes every Chrome, compositor, ffmpeg and Node child). Wall = monotonic clock from spawn to exit.
conditions: nice 19, idle ionice, CPUQuota=800% (8 of 16 threads). Shared server with production sites, CI VMs, other agents and a resident llama-server on the GPU. Rounds alternated between variants where noted.

windows.content: end of block 1, block 2 (presenter goes from full screen to a card, map on top), start of block 3

steps.label: Starting point: <OffthreadVideo>, JPEG sequence on disk, separate ffmpeg h264_nvenc
steps.note: Another pair of the same command under heavier load: 292.05 and 418.96 s CPU (mean 355.5, spread 36%).

steps.label: <Video> + MP4 straight from Remotion, h264_nvenc (--hardware-acceleration=required, 12 Mb/s)
steps.note: Same settings through the CLI directly: 119.89 and 110.75 s CPU, 31.03 and 27.07 s wall.

steps.label: Layers (P2): plan + graphics PNG + ffmpeg on GPU, one command
steps.note: Rounds alternated with the dedup variant. 1920x1080 version: 114.4 s CPU, 46.9 s wall (N=1).

steps.label: Layers + skip repeated frames (P3)
steps.note: 29% of frames reused (652 of 2241). 1920x1080 version: 101.0 s CPU, 43.1 s wall (N=1).

derived.note: Effect splits are the ones reported in the internal write-up for the 15 s segment: each removes one component from the bundle.

estimate_not_measured: Early estimates made before the cgroup measurement existed (for example about 1100 s of CPU for the whole of video R, or about 28 s of CPU per second of video) were projections from watching processes during a loaded render, not measurements. No figure or table uses them.
